g.text: One manager reviews six sample accounts, opens a case, and commits two interventions for the week.
+ Familiar flow for reviewing a full portfolio
+ Evidence and saved plan share one detail panel
Choose Ember + Cove: deadline and actionable issue.
Verify ID token; seed the six
Account docs with signals and plans
API confirms the save after commit
Starting evidence · sample day · ACV in USD · adoption = weekly active licensed users
Monitor; high value alone does not use a slot
Reconnect and investigate the usage decline
Align support owner and client on a resolution date
Request corrected report; retain unknown values
Confirm approver and decision date this week
Monitor until new evidence or renewal review
Cove has conflicting signals; Drift has a data gap.
Pick Ember and Cove; record why Cove goes ahead of Beacon.
Two slots used. Queue order follows renewal dates; ACV only breaks ties.
For Drift, record “More information needed”: usage report.
Saved without using a slot. Adoption still reads Unknown, not 0%.
For Cove, omit the owner. Attempt to save.
A labeled field explains the error; no incomplete plan is saved.
Set action: escalate issue; owner: Sam; follow-up: sample day + 2.
Reload: the plan, date and supporting evidence are still visible.
Resolve Cove’s issue. Inspect its attention reason.
Monitor: issue closed; 80% adoption and positive sponsor remain.
Trim shadcn-admin (React + Vite). Keep table, filters,
detail panel, accessible form and save feedback.
One workbench screen. Drop demo charts, chats, users and Clerk.
Keep the upstream MIT license and attribution.
Publish the static build on Vercel or GitHub Pages.
Use one root view; configure the Vite base for a Pages project path.
Both hosts call the same HTTPS API.
Go HTTP service on Cloud Run (us-central1), max-instances = 1.
POST session; PUT plan; PATCH signals. No read endpoint.
Verify the ID token on every call; take the UID only from it.
Validate input; commit slots and plan atomically; exact-origin CORS.
React subscribes to demos/{uid}/accounts in Firestore.
The first snapshot loads the queue. Changes update it in place.
Go writes through the server SDK. Rules allow the signed-in user
to read their own accounts. Deny client writes and detach on exit.
Re-attach the listener: its first snapshot is the saved state,
then updates follow. POST session is idempotent; no reseed.
Mark the live view stale if disconnected; the listener resumes from
the current snapshot. Confirm a save only after the API responds.
Unit prices · US dollars · November 2026 planning model
1 vCPU, 512 MiB; 0.2 billed seconds per request.
Default database in us-central1. Free quotas include 1 GiB
50k reads and 20k writes free daily. Overage per 100k:
Public static demo: 0.5 MB of assets per reviewer per month.
Hosting: $0 for an eligible public demo. Soft bandwidth limit:
100 GB/month. Commercial SaaS needs another host.
Five CDN requests per reviewer per month. At 100,000 reviewers:
500,000 requests and 50 GB of static assets.
Eligible personal Hobby demo: $0 within quotas.
Pro: from $20/month for one seat, plus applicable overages.
Occasional builds, small retained image and modest logs.
Assume available free quotas; these do not scale per user.
$0 assumed here. Excludes excess builds, images, logs,
API network egress, taxes, support and custom domains.
Monthly cost · core services (USD) · up to 100,000 monthly users
Attention rules · fixed thresholds · explainable checks, not predictions
Each monthly reviewer makes 100 API calls, reads 300 documents, writes 150, deletes 8 and receives 2 MiB from Firestore.
Reads include snapshots, updates, reconnects and transactions. Writes include seeds, plan edits and weekly capacity changes.
Assume traffic is evenly spread across 30 days and cleanup keeps average storage within 1 GiB, including indexes.
At 100,000 reviewers: 30M reads, 15M writes, 800k ordinary deletes and 195.31 GiB outbound. Americas transfer costs $0.12/GiB above 10 GiB.
Bursts, retries and longer retention can raise costs. Managed TTL, backups and point-in-time recovery are excluded.
¹ Choose one eligible host. Totals assume available free quotas and one Pro seat.
Buyer: head of customer success. Replace three spreadsheets with a single decision and follow-up workflow.
Missing data prompts investigation; a hypothesis stays labeled until verified. An information request uses no weekly slot.
The manager allocates both slots and records a reason; the app only orders the queue. ACV breaks ties and never triggers a rule.
Seed synthetic accounts per demo session. The React listener is the only read path; Go handles session start and every write. Owner follow-through is simulated.
Measure the share of accounts due this sample month with a dated, evidence-linked plan saved before renewal.
This measures planning coverage; it cannot establish that an intervention prevented churn.
Build order · every step leaves something that can ship
1 · Pure rule functions with boundary tests. 2 · Workbench screen on in-memory seed data. 3 · Write API with server-side validation.
4 · Listener and Firestore rules. 5 · Request limits and demo expiry.
API plus realtime is more than the 3–5 hour guide: stop after any step and state what is missing in the README.
No analytics, error monitoring or paid model on this board; the rule-based queue needs none of them.
Public demo safeguards · proposed controls and acceptance checks
Go verifies the Firebase ID token and derives the demo UID.
Firestore rules allow reads of that UID’s account documents
and deny all browser writes. Go authorizes every mutation.
Two tabs share live changes. An incognito session gets fresh seed
Another UID cannot read or edit the first session.
A Firestore transaction reads the weekly capacity document,
then saves the account plan and its slot together. An existing
account keeps its slot. A third distinct account gets 409.
Two tabs claim the last slot. One succeeds; the other gets 409 and
Retrying the winning save still uses just one slot.
Apply separate limits to session creation and plan writes. With
max-instances = 1 an in-memory limiter is enough;
move the counters to a shared store before raising the instance
When throttled, return 429 and Retry-After. Keep the form draft and
A write limit in Go does not meter Firestore listener reads.
Validate on the server: action from a fixed list, owner and notes
length-capped, follow-up date valid and on or before renewal, body
Errors return a code and a field name, never a stack trace. Logs
Omitting the owner returns 422 naming the field and stores nothing.
An unknown action or an oversized body is rejected.
A forced server error shows a generic message in the UI.
Expire inactive demos and measure stored bytes across sessions.
Blaze has no spending cap: set a budget alert
and keep max-instances = 1. Reprice if the assumptions in the cost
Check total document and index storage against 1 GiB and
outbound traffic against 10 GiB per month. Monitor daily
operation counts and verify that budget alerts are enabled.

Unknown is never read as 0% or as a fall
$100k Atlas stays here: ACV triggers no rule
A complete plan exists: action, owner and follow-up date
Missing owner: nothing saved, state unchanged
Review now, Needs information, Monitor; soonest renewal first; ACV breaks ties

Budget approval is pending seven days before Ember renews. Cove
has a critical issue its owner can escalate now.
Beacon waits despite a sharp usage drop. Revisit the
choice if its sponsor responds or Cove’s issue closes.
Managers can inspect the signal behind each flag. Drift’s failed
report stays visible as missing evidence.
Thresholds can miss gradual declines. The manager still
decides which two accounts get time.
Open one account at a time
A focused detail panel keeps the evidence beside the action,
Comparing Cove and Drift takes two visits. Revisit the
layout if managers repeatedly switch between them.
The API validates every change. A Firestore listener shows an
owner’s update in another tab without a refresh.
Two access paths need separate checks. Test API

A transaction saves the plan and reserves its slot together, even
when two tabs claim the last opening.
Concurrent edits for the same demo week can trigger
retries. Limit contention to that session and week.
